instructions:
OpenApiLuau generates typed Luau clients from OpenAPI 3 documents. The generator writes code that calls openapi-runtime, and other repositories install openapi-runtime and openapi-lute-transport as packages and commit the clients they generate. Review for impact on those generated clients as well as local correctness. In the summary, say whether generated code would change and whether existing generated clients keep working with the new runtime.

When the PR description links an issue, compare the diff with that issue and call out work it does not cover. When no issue is linked, say so in the summary without treating it as a defect.

Withhold a 5/5 score for defects and for high- or medium-severity rule violations. Leave low-severity rule notes as comments that do not lower the score.

rules.rule: When a change alters what openapi-runtime or openapi-lute-transport export from their init.luau, including function signatures, the Operation, Client, and Transport types, the ResponseKind and MultipartEncoding constants, or how send builds requests and reads responses, check that clients generated before the change still typecheck and behave the same. When a change alters the code the generator writes, such as function names, params types, or calls into the runtime, report it as a change to every generated client. A breaking change needs a .changes/ entry with a major bump and the breaking flag.

openapi-runtime stays free of runtime-specific APIs so a client can run anywhere a transport exists. Flag a require of @std, @lute, or a Roblox service in workspace/openapi-runtime. HTTP and JSON belong in a transport.

Other repositories vendor openapi-runtime and openapi-lute-transport, so code inside them requires its own modules with relative paths or @self. Flag a require through a repo alias such as @workspace, @repo, or @lpm inside those two packages.

When a change renames a symbol, changes a value, or fixes a bug that a skill in flipbook-labs/agent-skills describes, name the skill that now needs updating. That fix lands in agent-skills, so this is a follow-up note for the author.

Comments explain why the code is the way it is now, for a reader who never saw an earlier version. Flag comments that only make sense against a past shape of the code, such as ones that say what the code 'used to' do, what happened 'previously', or where logic 'moved to'.

New or changed production behavior needs a test that would fail without the change, as a colocated *.spec.luau. Refactors that keep behavior the same don't need new specs. A change to the code the generator writes needs generate.spec.luau or another spec to show the new output. Flag tests that only restate what the implementation returns, mock the module under test, or cannot fail.
Check logic belongs in .lute/ scripts that workflows call, not inline in workflow YAML. Action pinning and job timeouts follow org/repo-conventions in flipbook-labs/agent-skills.

Do not add new install-time patches to upstream packages. Flag a change that rewrites files under .lpm/ after they are installed. A problem in an upstream package gets an issue filed with that package instead.

A PR adds at most one .changes/ entry. Its summary is one short sentence, about 140 characters at most, in present tense, with no references to PRs, branches, or how the change was developed. Developers read this changelog, so naming the affected API is welcome. Its category comes from changewrite.luau, and its kind names the package it touches: Generator, Runtime, Transport, or Tooling.
